ideas.risks: May fail if the original policy model lets delayed trade feedback carry information not already contained in public prices and private randomness; null-set conventions could force a completed-measure rather than Borel statement.
ideas.summary: Prove that every admissible private-randomized Borel policy in the public exogenous model induces law-independent public-prefix marginal kernels q_t(P_1:t) on a finite quote grid, with identical expected reward coordinates L_theta.
ideas.title: Policy-to-kernel alignment
ideas.why_promising: This is the main remaining gap between the accepted completed L-infinity kernel no-gap theorem and the original policy model.

ideas.risks: Borel representatives may not exist simultaneously for all dominating measures without changing the policy class; the clean theorem may need to be stated on completed measurable spaces only.
ideas.summary: Starting from a completed L-infinity(lambda_t; Delta(G)) prefix kernel, determine exact assumptions under which it has an admissible Borel or completed-measurable implementation preserving all payoff-weighted integrals.
ideas.title: Kernel implementation lemma
ideas.why_promising: It isolates the reverse alignment issue and could make the infinite-class domination theorem referee-ready or identify the exact model restriction needed.

ideas.risks: The measure-density formula must be matched to regular conditional probabilities carefully on mixture-prefix null sets; strict threshold nonattainment should stay avoided by finite G.
ideas.summary: Prove that the density support formula integral max_a sum_theta pi_theta f^theta_{t,a} d lambda_t equals the conditional Bayes envelope E max_a a P_bar_pi(M_t > a | P_1:t) for every finite prior under reward-measure domination.
ideas.title: Density Psi identification
ideas.why_promising: This would connect the compactness/no-gap proof to the already accepted Psi_G,F expression without relying on informal conditional-probability manipulations.

ideas.risks: Revealing labels can accidentally change delay profiles if inserted at a payoff-relevant time or price level; the construction must keep comparator rewards and truncation losses literally matched.
ideas.summary: Build paired classes with identical per-world beta, Delta, and delta profiles but different minimax regret: a hidden q-scaled terminal pair versus the same pair with a harmless public label revealed before the first decision.
ideas.title: Tail-profile no-go pair
ideas.why_promising: A clean example would prove that no scalar condition depending only on individual delay or truncation tails can characterize unknown-class learnability; observability/predictability is essential.

ideas.risks: Naive block repetition collapses because the comparator is a single fixed quote; information may also accumulate too quickly after early reveals.
ideas.summary: Use the finite-grid Psi value to search for multi-scale or limited-leakage lower-bound families under beta or Delta envelopes, aiming to accumulate delayed Bayes gaps across scales without iid comparator collapse.
ideas.title: Power-tail lower rates
ideas.why_promising: Matching the truncation upper rate is the largest open quantitative gap, and Psi_G gives a precise diagnostic for whether a proposed construction actually has large minimax value.

ideas.risks: A meta-algorithm may pay extra delay overhead for every window, and comparator-gap terms for different H may not combine cleanly.
ideas.summary: Design an adaptive multi-window algorithm that competes with the best truncation level in hindsight, targeting a bound like inf_H {sqrt(T H log K) + T/K + delta_T(H)} plus small overhead.
ideas.title: Adaptive truncation upper bound
ideas.why_promising: It would turn the sufficient theorem into a sharper rate formula that does not require knowing the tail profile in advance and may expose whether the current upper bound is loose.

ideas.risks: A doubling or horizon-mixture version of the known-law oracle may defeat the proposed obstruction; the benchmark varies with the evaluation horizon and must be handled exactly.
ideas.summary: Formalize or refute the super-growing two-deadline deterministic sequence as an anytime known-law obstruction, separating horizon-aware oracle learnability from single-policy learnability over all T.
ideas.title: Anytime known-law boundary
ideas.why_promising: It resolves an important quantifier ambiguity left by the oracle lemma and clarifies whether fixed-law necessity becomes nontrivial again without horizon awareness.

ideas.risks: Natural examples may all be either identifiable or dominated enough for no-gap; remaining gaps may be purely pathological measurability artifacts.
ideas.summary: Search for a standard-Borel, nondominated, non-identifiable infinite class where finite subclasses have small value but the full Borel-policy class has linear value, or prove broad identifiable/analytic no-gap conditions.
ideas.title: Natural infinite-class gaps
ideas.why_promising: This tests whether product-closed or domination hypotheses are merely technical or genuinely necessary beyond the current non-Borel obstruction.
